novelty_flags.label: Theorems 1–2 / related-work survey
novelty_flags.one_line: Add and compare Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié (2018), a public non-archival working paper claiming sharp ATE bounds under finite unconditional moment restrictions; it is materially closer to the cone-completion kernel, though its unavailable comparison alone does not establish prior-art subsumption.

soundness_flags.label: Definitions of W_i, omega(P'), H_n, and Theorem 4
soundness_flags.one_line: The model permits treatment arms outside {d,e}, but l_a,u_a and bounded-support assumptions are supplied only for target arms, so l_{D_i}, u_{D_i}, W_i, and the claimed [0,1] bounded moments are undefined or unbounded on non-target observed cells; restrict to A={d,e} or impose known ranges and factual support for every observed arm.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the sampling/inference submodel binary-treatment, or extend the endpoint and bounded-support primitives to every observed treatment arm before defining W_i and the primitive confidence region.

Add Kédagni–Li–Mourifié (2018) to related work and compare its finite unconditional-moment sharp set theorem-by-theorem with the proposed exact-support completion problem; state explicitly whether its class excludes the proposal's SDC/BoS class or is subsumed by it.

Strengthen the field case beyond one rational strict example by proving an open nondegenerate family of observed laws on which the Ban–Kédagni normalized outer union is strictly wider than the exact-support closure.
Turn the adaptive-inference OEQ into a slack-indexed theorem with an explicit rate and matching two-point or local-asymptotic lower frontier away from zero slack.

recommended_next_step: Repair the multivalued-treatment primitive-moment defect and complete the Kédagni–Li–Mourifié comparison; then retain the sharp exact-support cone kernel as a field-tier Stage-0 target.
